examples.ko: 아빠! 이번 주말에 놀이동산에 놀러 가요.
examples.en: Dad! Let's go to the amusement park this weekend.

examples.ko: 놀이동산은 사람이 너무 많아서 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: The amusement park is so crowded that the lines are long.
Yesterday I rode a roller coaster at the amusement park.
The kids keep begging to go to the amusement park.
I bought an all-day pass for the amusement park with my friend.
I watched a parade inside the amusement park.

explain: 롤러코스터, 회전목마 같은 놀이기구가 있는 곳이에요. '놀이공원'이라고도 말해서 둘 다 알아 두면 좋아요. '놀이동산에 가다', '놀이동산에서 놀다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm going to the amusement park this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀이동산'과 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 놀이동산, and both are common.

phrases.en: On Children's Day, we went to the amusement park to have fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀러 가다'와 함께 써서 즐기러 가는 느낌을 내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 놀러 가다, it conveys going to have fun.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to an amusement park for fun

phrases.en: We played at the amusement park all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 '에서'를 붙여 거기서 시간을 보낸다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 에서, it says where you spent your time.
phrases.en_equiv: to play at an amusement park

explain_en: It is a place with rides such as roller coasters and carousels. People also say '놀이공원', so it is good to know both. You say '놀이동산에 가다' or '놀이동산에서 놀다'.

examples.en: On a wet road, a bicycle can slip.
When driving in the rain, you have to slow down.
I was late for the appointment because of the rainy roads.
The car skidded while driving on the wet road.
Please go home carefully on the rainy roads after work.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘 빗길이 많이 미끄러워요.
examples.en: It's raining, so the roads are very slippery today.

explain: '빗길 운전', '빗길 교통사고'처럼 뉴스와 안전 안내에 자주 나와요. 비슷한 짝말로 '눈길', '빙판길'이 있어요. 발음은 [비낄] 또는 [빋낄]이에요.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 오면 빗길 교통사고가 늘어요.
phrases.en: When it rains a lot, traffic accidents on wet roads increase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안전 안내에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in news and safety notices.

phrases.en: The bus slipped on the rainy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 때문에 젖은 길에서 미끄러질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something slips on a road wet from rain.
phrases.en_equiv: to slip on a rainy road

phrases.en: I drove slowly on the rainy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 오는 길을 차나 사람이 지나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a car or person moving along a road in the rain.
phrases.en_equiv: to drive on a rainy road

explain_en: It often appears in news and safety notices, as in '빗길 운전' and '빗길 교통사고'. Similar words are '눈길' (snowy road) and '빙판길' (icy road). It is pronounced [비낄] or [빋낄].

examples.en: That family lives on a remote island.

examples.ko: 배를 타고 한 시간 가면 외딴섬이 나와요.
examples.en: If you go an hour by boat, you reach a remote island.
There are no shops or hospitals on the remote island.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 외딴섬에 혼자 남았어요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie was left alone on a remote island.

examples.ko: 외딴섬이라서 날씨가 나쁘면 배가 안 떠요.
examples.en: It's a remote island, so boats don't run in bad weather.

examples.ko: 외딴섬으로 여행을 가 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever traveled to a remote island?

explain: '외딴'은 다른 곳과 떨어져 있다는 뜻이고 '외딴집', '외딴곳'에도 써요. 사람이 거의 없고 오가기 힘든 섬을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 영화나 소설의 배경으로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It's a small village in a remote place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 섬이 아니라 다른 곳과 떨어진 장소 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to any remote place, not only an island.

phrases.en: An old woman lives alone in an isolated house in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 집과 떨어져 혼자 있는 집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A house standing alone, far from other houses.

phrases.en: I went to a remote island by boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외딴섬'에 조사와 동사를 붙여 쓴 가장 쉬운 문장 틀이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple sentence pattern that adds a particle and verb to 외딴섬.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a remote island

explain_en: '외딴' means set apart from other places and also appears in '외딴집' and '외딴곳'. It suits an island with few people and hard to reach. It often appears as a setting in movies and novels.

examples.ko: 이 버스는 새벽 다섯 시부터 운행해요.
examples.en: This bus runs from five in the morning.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 열차가 운행하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The train didn't run because of the heavy rain.
Does the subway run until midnight?
Is there a bus that goes to the airport?

examples.ko: 눈 때문에 오늘은 운행할 수 없대요.
examples.en: They say it can't run today because of the snow.

examples.ko: 새 기차가 다음 달부터 운행해서 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: A new train starts running next month, so it will be more convenient.

explain: 버스, 기차, 지하철, 배 같은 교통수단이 정해진 길을 다닌다고 할 때 써요. 사람이 차를 모는 것은 주로 '운전하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The subway runs until midnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통수단이 주어이고 다닌다는 사실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the vehicle as subject to say that it runs.

phrases.en: This bus runs every fifteen minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '운행하다'보다 쉬운 '다니다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, the easier 다니다 is used more than 운행하다.

phrases.en: Please tell me the bus operating hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통수단이 다니는 시간을 말할 때 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the hours a vehicle is in service.

explain_en: Use it when a bus, train, subway, or ship runs along a set route. A person driving a car is usually '운전하다'.

gh: passive: buses or trains are in service

examples.en: Please watch the road ahead and drive carefully.
There is construction ahead, so please go slowly.
My older brother was in a frontline unit in the army.

examples.ko: 차의 카메라가 전방의 사고 장면을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The car's camera recorded the accident scene ahead.
The road ahead is blocked, so the cars aren't moving.
It is dangerous if you do not keep watching the road ahead.

explain: 앞쪽을 가리키는 딱딱한 말이라 도로 표지판, 설명서, 뉴스에서 봐요. 일상에서는 그냥 '앞'이라고 해요. 군대에서는 휴전선 가까이 있는 곳도 '전방'이라고 불러요. 반대는 '후방'이에요.

phrases.en: Watching the road ahead is important when driving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전할 때 앞을 잘 보라는 안내에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair often seen in driving safety notices about watching ahead.

phrases.en: There is an accident ahead, so the road is blocked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 앞쪽 위치를 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에, it marks a place ahead.

phrases.en: There are many cars up front.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전방'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 전방 and more natural in everyday talk.

explain_en: A stiff word for the front side, seen on road signs, manuals, and in the news. In daily speech people simply say '앞'. In the military it also names areas near the armistice line. The opposite is '후방' (rear).

dis.h: forward area ahead; formal or military
gh: basic word: in front of, ahead
front side of a flat object

p.n: 앞 is plain and casual; 전방 sounds formal or written.

examples.en: Lots of cargo trucks run on the highway.

examples.ko: 화물차 한 대가 짐을 싣고 있어요.
examples.en: A cargo truck is loading goods.

examples.ko: 화물차는 이 길로 다니면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Cargo trucks must not use this road.
The cargo truck driver unloaded the goods for us.
On moving day I rented a small cargo truck.

examples.ko: 새벽에는 화물차 소리 때문에 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up at dawn because of the sound of cargo trucks.

explain: '트럭'이라고도 많이 불러요. 법이나 뉴스에서는 '화물차', 일상에서는 '트럭'이 더 흔해요. 아주 작은 것은 '소형 트럭'이나 '1톤 트럭'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My uncle drives a truck.
phrases.nuance_ko: '화물차'와 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '트럭'이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 화물차; 트럭 is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: My father works as a cargo truck driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화물차를 운전하는 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the job of driving a cargo truck.

phrases.en: A big cargo truck came onto the narrow road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사를 앞에 붙여 화물차의 크기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an adjective in front to describe the size of the truck.

explain_en: People often say '트럭' (truck) too. Laws and the news use 화물차, while daily conversation uses 트럭 more. A very small one is called a '소형 트럭' (small truck) or a '1톤 트럭' (1-ton truck).

examples.en: That singer's high notes are powerful and clear.

examples.ko: 고음을 낼 때 목이 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: Your throat can hurt when you hit high notes.
The high-note part of this song is hard.
The sound got thinner as it went higher.
I am worried my voice will crack on the high notes.

examples.ko: 저는 고음은 잘 못 내지만 저음은 자신 있어요.
examples.en: I cannot hit high notes well, but I am confident with low ones.

explain: '저음'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 노래방에서는 높은 음을 못 내는 사람이 '고음 불가'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: That singer hits high notes well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 소리를 목으로 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for producing a high note with one's voice.

phrases.en: I have a cold, so I can't reach the high notes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 소리를 내지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you cannot produce high notes.

phrases.en: At karaoke, I can't sing high notes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농담처럼 가볍게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light, joking expression.

explain_en: It pairs with 저음. At karaoke, people who cannot reach high notes sometimes joke '고음 불가'.

examples.en: I stopped walking in front of the cliff.
The side of the road was a steep drop, so I was scared.
I had a dream of falling off a cliff.
Please don't go toward the cliff edge.
There are many steep drops on the mountain trail, so be careful.
You can see the sea below the cliff.

explain: '절벽'은 높고 가파른 바위 벽 자체를 말하고, '낭떠러지'는 그 끝에서 아래로 떨어지는 위험한 곳을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다', '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'처럼 써요. 위험한 상황을 비유할 때도 나와요.

phrases.en: In the movie, a car fell off a cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳에서 아래로 떨어지는 위험한 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dangerous situation of falling from a high place.

phrases.en: Please don't go to the edge of the cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 가장자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about the dangerous edge.

phrases.en: There is a high cliff by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바위 벽 자체를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for the rock wall itself.

explain_en: '절벽' is the steep rock wall itself, while '낭떠러지' feels natural when you mean the dangerous drop at the edge. You say '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다' or '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'. It can also be used figuratively for a dangerous situation.

examples.en: I record my favorite drama.
I recorded the class and watched it again later.
I recorded the game, but there's no sound.
Please be quiet while we're recording.

examples.ko: 방송을 녹화하려면 먼저 저장 공간을 확인하세요.
examples.en: If you want to record a broadcast, check the storage space first.
May I record the presentation?

explain: 녹화하다는 영상을 기록해 두는 거예요. 소리만 기록하는 것은 '녹음하다'예요. '생방송'과 반대로, 미리 녹화한 방송은 '녹화 방송'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This program is a recorded broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생방송과 반대로, 미리 찍은 방송을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of a live broadcast; a pre-recorded show.

phrases.en: I'll record the game and keep it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'로 나중에 보려고 미리 해 놓는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아/어 두다 means doing it in advance for later.

phrases.en: When the camera turns on, recording starts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상을 찍기 시작할 때 '녹화'와 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 녹화 when video recording begins.

explain_en: 녹화하다 is to record video. Recording sound only is '녹음하다', so keep them apart. In contrast to a '생방송' (live broadcast), a pre-recorded program is a '녹화 방송'.
